body:
Three documents, three lenses, and one point of flat convergence: if engagement fails at every lower level, stop treating this as a chore problem and ask whether the living arrangement still fits. The account reaches it as step 5, the rival as r11, and the objection contests neither. Three framings landing on the same terminus is weak but real evidence the terminus is right, so I keep that step and promote it from afterthought to named endpoint.

What I take from the objection. First, o2 is right, and I revise the account's central test accordingly: falling recurrence on specified chores is consistent with every hypothesis on the table, including a lopsided arrangement with clearer paperwork. The account's stated consequence — recurrence falls, so the ambiguity hypothesis is supported — is rejected as written. Recurrence is data, but not discriminating data. Second, o3 is right that thin material licenses probes, not an ordering; I reject the presentation of the five steps as the natural sequence while keeping most of the steps as moves. But I do not follow the objection all the way to re-ordering around the conversational-form reading on its own terms, because of its own o4 and the rival's own r9: from this material, no ordering is earned. What is earned is a different selection criterion. The hypotheses are stackable rather than exclusive — the agreements can be genuinely vague and the load uneven and one flatmate allergic to obligatory framings — so moves should be chosen for robustness across readings and for diagnostic yield, not for confidence in one reading.

What I take from the rival. The single most useful contribution in all three documents is r7: watch how the withdrawing flatmate responds to a specification proposal — engaging with its content, or pulling back from the very idea of a written arrangement. That converts the account's weak confirmation test into an actual discriminator, and it bolts onto the account's own machinery. I also take r8 (owned zones, default-outcome rotations) but as a contingent fallback, with the objection's c2 attached: zones can quietly entrench an uneven load, so if adopted they should be framed as a truce about exposure, not presented as the fair settlement.

What I revise. The rival's r6 as literally phrased — open by asking each flatmate what they think the flat is — I reject as an opener. From a fellow tenant rather than a mediator it will often land as a philosophy exam or an accusation, and it forces a dichotomy the friend may not recognize as theirs. The information it wants is real; the elicitation is wrong. Instead, the account's step 4 and the rival's r6 merge into one first move: ten minutes, one-to-one, explicitly not a prelude to a group settlement, organized around the axis the objection and rival both surfaced: 'I've noticed you've gone quiet about house stuff. I'm not trying to drag you back to a meeting. Is it the chores, or is it the way the conversations keep going?' That question is robust across every hypothesis: whichever reading is true, the answer is evidence, and the asking itself is the re-entry the account wanted.

The spec probe stays second, redesigned from remedy into instrument: propose written specs for two or three recurring items, then observe on two channels — recurrence, and mode of engagement per r7 — plus the objection's predicted signature that complaints migrate to new items or resurge after the next schedule change. Content-engagement plus falling recurrence supports ambiguity; migration supports renegotiation or legitimacy; pullback-from-the-idea supports the unit-versus-privacy reading; and a flat 'no point writing it down, nothing changes' would be evidence of something all three documents underweight: agreements being made without expectation of being kept.

One thing no input examines: the asker's standpoint. All three write as though the reader were an experimenter running probes on the household. The reader is a party, and plausibly the convening one. If the friend is avoiding conversations, some of what is avoided may be conversations with the asker specifically, and any probe the asker runs will be read partly as a message about the asker. So the one-to-one should include a survivable version of 'is there something about how I raise this that makes it worse?', and the asker should expect the probe to return evidence about themselves.

What stays open: which reading is right; whether the load has in fact been uneven (both account and rival gesture at this without evidence); how long this has run. The merged plan is built to be useful without those answers and to produce some of them. Firmly rejected: recurrence-as-confirmation, the rival's opener phrasing, hypothesis-exclusivity, and — now with more confidence, since both objection and rival imply a group setting would suppress exactly the signal needed — the single big meeting.
